subject: Finaptic — integration & auth recap + next steps
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference.com>
To: Aiden Brooks <aiden.brooks@finaptic.ai>, Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@finaptic.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Finaptic — integration & auth recap + next steps

Thanks again for your time this morning — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Integration scope (what we covered)
- SDK bootstrapping: language SDKs (Python/Node) + container option for on-prem testing
- Auth options: API keys for service-to-service calls, short-lived JWTs for user flows, and a recommended service-account model for embeddings pipelines
- Routing & model variants: prefix-based routing for low-latency flows, fallback route to cheaper quantized models for background jobs
- Structured output / tool-calling: intent -> tool mapping and JSON schema validation on response
- Embeddings & rerankers: per-customer indexing, vector store choices, and a suggested reranker model for high-precision searches

2) Security & key mgmt details we propose
- Primary pattern: Service Account + short-lived JWTs minted by your auth tier (recommended 1h lifetime) to avoid long-lived secrets in apps.
- Keys: use KMS-backed signing key (we support our KMS integrations or bring-your-own HSM).
- API keys: allowed for internal CI/automation only, with enforced IP & route scoping.
- Rotation: automated rotation cadence suggested at 30–90 days depending on sensitivity; we can provide a key-rotation webhook for your pipeline.

3) Action items (owner / ETA)
- Aiden: confirm whether Finaptic will use an internal KMS or prefer Redwood-managed KMS (reply by 2027-05-06)
- Hannah: send integration notes + sample JWT minting snippet (attached) — done (see attachment)
- Marcus / Laura: prepare a short demo plan (30m) showing embeddings + reranking with a test dataset — target 2027-05-11

Attachments: redwood-integration-notes.pdf (auth snippets, SDK examples), finaptic-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (M.A.P. with milestones)

If that all looks right I’ll schedule the 30m demo for next Tuesday at 10am PT — otherwise propose a time.

Cheers,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt

Thanks Hannah — helpful notes. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we lock the demo: 

- KMS: we plan to use our cloud KMS (GCP KMS) for signing if Redwood supports OIDC/JWK rotation endpoints. Can you confirm the rotation webhook and JWK exposure pattern?
- API keys: good to know you prefer limiting API keys to CI. For our SRE automation we’ll likely need a scoped machine account — can that be restricted per-route (embeddings only)?
- JWT lifetime: 1h is fine for interactive UI. For background indexing jobs we’d prefer a slightly longer TTL (4h) if we use short-lived tokens. Is there a recommended approach for background workers?

Also — can Marcus/Laura include a small sample index (500 records) we can use in the demo? We’ll upload a sanitized dataset after you confirm the demo window.

Best,
Aiden Brooks
Head of Platform Engineering | Finaptic
aiden.brooks@finaptic.ai

Hannah — quick internal notes before the demo: 

- JWK / rotation: Redwood can expose a JWK set URL per-customer and provide a rotation webhook so your KMS can push new keys. For Finaptic’s GCP KMS we’ll accept a signed key upload or federated OIDC trust. I’ll add the exact endpoints to the demo deck.
- Route scoping: we support tag-based route policies. Marcus: we should propose \"embeddings-only\" route keys for Finaptic's automation. That enforces per-route rate limits and cost buckets.
- Background workers: recommend a two-token pattern — a short-lived worker token (4h) with limited scope + refresh via a service account that uses KMS-signed grants. This avoids embedding long-lived secrets in the worker image.
- Audit & logs: Finaptic asked about audit retention — default 90 days; enterprise retention options available. Note for procurement.

I’ll draft 3 slides: auth flow diagrams, sample curl + SDK snippets for JWT minting, and recommended rotation cadence matrix (30/60/90).

-Marcus

Solutions Engineering Manager | Redwood Inference
